sourceRefs: Written after a live debugging session on 2026-08-04 tracing a real multi-hour dispatch stall
Corrects a stale assumption that poll_workers was never decomposed (it was, in supervisor-rewrite memory) -- verified live against current source

acceptance: Read docs/04/supervisor_dispatch_refactor_proposal_2026-08-04.md section 'Problem 2' for full context before starting.

Add scripts/explain_dispatch.py <task-id> [--agent <agent-id>] that composes the EXISTING pure gate functions in .orchestrator/supervisor.py (agent_auto_dispatch_block_reason, task_execution_dispatch_candidate, agent_can_take_task, quota_group_concurrency_limit, agent_dispatch_capacity, dependencies_satisfied, task_assignment_is_catalog_locked, dispatch_event_is_in_unchanged_cooldown) in the exact order dispatch_ready_tasks evaluates them.

For the given task, evaluate every currently-enabled agent and print a structured trace: which gate returned a blocking verdict first and its exact reason string, or 'no blocking gate found' if none did.

Read-only: must not mutate config.json, state, or provider_capabilities.json. Must not require the canonical task-state lock (use the same read-only loading pattern as read_only_commands in scripts/ai_status.py).
Add unit tests covering at least: capability-blocked agent, quota-exhausted agent, capacity-exhausted agent, catalog-locked task, unmet dependency, cooldown-suppressed event, and the all-clear case.
Do not touch poll_workers, process_queue, or reconcile_queue_records.
task_spec.summary: Composes existing pure dispatch-gate functions into a single read-only CLI that answers 'why was task X not dispatched this tick' without hand-writing a throwaway script against internal functions, as had to be done live on 2026-08-04.
task_spec.title: Add a dispatch-explain diagnostic tool for supervisor.py

acceptance: Read docs/04/supervisor_dispatch_refactor_proposal_2026-08-04.md section 'Problem 1' for full context, including the confirmed live repro (agy/claude flipping to 'not installed' under load_1m ~3-4 within seconds of a healthy probe, same binaries, same PATH, no state change).

load_provider_report's default auto_refresh_provider_capabilities=true currently re-invokes live CLI binaries synchronously inside dispatch_ready_tasks's call path every cycle. Move probing to its own timer/tick, independent of the dispatch cycle; dispatch must read the last good cached provider_capabilities.json with a configurable staleness bound and never trigger a live probe itself.

Add hysteresis: an agent's can_auto_deliver must only flip from true to false after N consecutive failed probes (configurable, default suggestion 2-3), not one. Flipping false to true may remain immediate.

When a probe result's effective can_auto_deliver actually changes (not just re-confirms the same value), emit a distinct activity-log event type (e.g. provider_capability_transitioned) with old/new state and the raw probe failure detail, instead of only being visible by diffing provider_capabilities.json.

Use scripts/explain_dispatch.py (SUP-DISPATCH-EXPLAIN-TOOL-20260804) to verify: force a synthetic single-probe failure and confirm dispatch is NOT blocked (hysteresis holds), then force N consecutive failures and confirm it IS blocked with the transition event present.
Shadow-verify against current behavior per the rewrite/shadow.py discipline before cutover; ship behind a flag, incumbent one flag away, consistent with every other SUPERVISOR-REWRITE phase.
task_spec.summary: The single highest-value fix from the 2026-08-04 session: a flaky, auto-refreshing, inline capability probe silently zeroed out dispatch for Claude/Claude2/Antigravity for hours because one transient CLI timeout under load was treated as ground truth with no debounce and no visible signal.
task_spec.title: Decouple provider capability probing from the dispatch hot path and add failure hysteresis

acceptance: Read docs/04/supervisor_dispatch_refactor_proposal_2026-08-04.md section 'Problem 4' for full context, including the confirmed live repro (boot reconciliation retried SUP-L12-GUARDED-REMEDIATION-CATALOG-CORRECTION-20260803 four times then gave up with worker_failed, while the task record stayed at its original todo/last_update with zero visible trace).
Add a failure_streak integer field directly on the task record, incremented on worker_failed, reset to 0 on worker_completed or a successful review/handoff transition.

Past a configured threshold (reuse or align with existing SUP-L12-STALE-FAILURE-STREAK-REAPER conventions already in this codebase), transition the task to an explicit status: "quarantined" rather than leaving it silently stuck at its prior status.
A quarantined task must require an explicit operator or auto-worker action (e.g. reopen) to clear, and that action must reset failure_streak.
This is purely additive to the task schema; must not change any existing gate's pass/fail behavior for tasks below the threshold.
Add tests for: streak increments on repeated failure, reset on success, quarantine transition at threshold, and that quarantine blocks normal ready-dispatch pickup until cleared.
task_spec.summary: Makes repeated dispatch failure visible on the board itself instead of only in raw activity-log JSONL, closing the exact gap that made SUP-L12-GUARDED-REMEDIATION-CATALOG-CORRECTION-20260803 indistinguishable from an untouched task after 5 failed attempts.
task_spec.title: Add a failure_streak counter and quarantined status to the task schema

acceptance: Read docs/04/supervisor_dispatch_refactor_proposal_2026-08-04.md section 'Problem 3' for full context, including the confirmed live repro (ActivityAuditInvariantError: 'activity content-addressed archives do not match lineage', transient, tied to a concurrency burst right after a supervisor restart, which silently dropped a worker's status write-back with zero trace on the task record).

Do not weaken _validate_active_lineage_head_unlocked or any other fail-closed integrity check itself -- the guarantee is real and intentional (see the original PR #4221 incident this protects against).

Extend the existing outbox concept (STATUS_ARCHIVE_OUTBOX_KEY / STATUS_ACTIVITY_OUTBOX_KEY) so that a status write which cannot clear the integrity check is durably queued for retry AND marks the task itself (e.g. status_write_pending: true plus a pending count), rather than leaving the task record byte-identical to its pre-attempt state.

A human or auto-worker reading the board must be able to distinguish 'this task's displayed state may be stale, N writes queued behind an integrity block' from 'this task genuinely has not been touched.'

This touches the exact mechanism responsible for a prior 4-hour production outage (see SUPERVISOR_REWRITE_PLAN.md motivation). Shadow-verify behavior-equivalence against the incumbent per rewrite/shadow.py discipline before any cutover; ship behind a flag.
Land only after SUP-PROVIDER-PROBE-HYSTERESIS-20260804 and SUP-TASK-FAILURE-STREAK-SCHEMA-20260804 are merged, per the risk-based sequencing in the proposal doc.
task_spec.summary: Closes the gap where a transient, already-self-resolving integrity check failure left a task's board record indistinguishable from one that was never dispatched at all -- the highest-risk of the four fixes since it touches the same mechanism a prior real outage came from, so it is sequenced last and gated on the other two landing first.
task_spec.title: Make activity-log-integrity-blocked status writes durable and visible instead of silently dropped
